/-!
# Conjecture 10.35

by G. A. Noskov

Is it true that every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$ is
residually in the class of torsion-free subgroups of $GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$?

Here $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$, and a group is
*torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity. A group $G$ is
*residually in a class* $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups if for every $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$ there
is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $g \notin N$ and $G/N \in \mathfrak{X}$; equivalently, the
normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{X}$ intersect trivially. Since the class of
torsion-free subgroups of $GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ is closed under isomorphism and under
taking subgroups, $G$ is residually in this class exactly when every $g \neq 1$ in $G$ has a
nontrivial image under some homomorphism from $G$ to a torsion-free subgroup of
$GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

For non-commutative groups this is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`, which asks that
$x \mapsto x^k$ be injective for every $k \neq 0$ (the "unique roots" property); the two
agree for commutative groups.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsMulTorsionFree (Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs) — rejected because it is the unique-roots property, not torsion-freeness, for non-commutative groups; Monoid.IsTorsion (the dual notion, not applicable).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.35».IsTorsionFreeGroup
justification.why_needed: 'Torsion-free group' = only the identity has finite order. Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (the current replacement for the old `Monoid.IsTorsionFree` def, whose stale mention survives in GroupTheory/Torsion.lean's header) requires x ↦ xⁿ to be injective for all n ≠ 0, i.e. the unique-roots (R-group) property; `isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder` holds only for `CommGroup`. For non-abelian linear groups this is strictly stronger (e.g. the Klein bottle group ⟨a,b | aba⁻¹ = b⁻¹⟩ is torsion-free but (ab)² = a²), so using it would change both the hypothesis on G and the target class. Defined as `∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder g`, with two API lemmas (implied by IsMulTorsionFree; inherited by subgroups).

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isTorsionFreeGroup_iff_isMulTorsionFree (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] :
    IsTorsionFreeGroup G ↔ IsMulTorsionFree G := by
  rw [isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder]
  exact ⟨fun h a ha hfin => ha (h a hfin), fun h a hfin => by_contra fun hne => h hne hfin⟩

Is it true that every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$ is
residually in the class of torsion-free subgroups of $GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$?

That is, for every $n$ and every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup $G$ of

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question: for every n and every finitely generated torsion-free G ≤ GL_n(ℂ), for each g ≠ 1 in G there is a homomorphism φ : G → H with H a torsion-free subgroup of GL_n(Q̄) (same n; Q̄ the algebraic numbers, e.g. the algebraic closure of ℚ inside ℂ) and φ(g) ≠ 1 — surjectivity of φ is immaterial since the class is closed under subgroups, and 'residually' means the intersection of the kernels of such homomorphisms is trivial.
claims.reviewer_why: c07 (with c02/c05 essentially identical in substance) is the faithful formalization: for every n and every finitely generated subgroup G ≤ GL_n(ℂ) with no nontrivial element of finite order, each g ≠ 1 in G is separated by a homomorphism into some subgroup H ≤ GL_n(Q̄) that has no nontrivial element of finite order (same n; Q̄ = AlgebraicClosure ℚ, harmless since the property only depends on GL_n(Q̄) up to isomorphism; surjectivity immaterial since the class is subgroup-closed). Final file uses c07's theorem shape and bespoke predicate (renamed/defined as ∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1, as in c02/c05), plus proven API lemmas relating it to Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree. Candidates c01, c03, c04, c06, c08 were rejected: they use Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`, which is the unique-roots property (a ↦ a^k injective for all k ≠ 0); Mathlib only proves it equivalent to 'no nontrivial element of finite order' under `CommGroup`. For non-abelian linear groups — exactly the setting of this problem — it is strictly stronger (e.g. the Klein-bottle group ⟨a,b | aba⁻¹=b⁻¹⟩ ≤ GL_3(ℤ) is f.g. torsion-free but (ab)² = a² with ab ≠ a), so those candidates change both the hypothesis on G and the target class, altering the mathematical claim.

/-!
# Conjecture 10.35

by G. A. Noskov

Is it true that every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$ is
residually in the class of torsion-free subgroups of $GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$?

Here $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$, and a group is

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«10.35»

/--
A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

For non-commutative groups this is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`, which asks that
$x \mapsto x^k$ be injective for every $k \neq 0$ (the "unique roots" property); the two
agree for commutative groups.
-/
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- A group with unique roots (Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`) is torsion-free. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsTorsionFreeGroup.of_isMulTorsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulTorsionFree G] :
    IsTorsionFreeGroup G :=
  fun _ hg => by_contra fun h => not_isOfFinOrder_of_isMulTorsionFree h hg

/-- For commutative groups, being torsion-free is the same as `IsMulTorsionFree`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isTorsionFreeGroup_iff_isMulTorsionFree (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] :
    IsTorsionFreeGroup G ↔ IsMulTorsionFree G := by
  rw [isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder]
  exact ⟨fun h a ha hfin => ha (h a hfin), fun h a hfin => by_contra fun hne => h hne hfin⟩

/-- Subgroups of torsion-free groups are torsion-free. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsTorsionFreeGroup.subgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsTorsionFreeGroup G)
    (H : Subgroup G) : IsTorsionFreeGroup H :=
  fun g hg => Subtype.ext (hG g (H.subtype.isOfFinOrder hg))

/--
Is it true that every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$ is
residually in the class of torsion-free subgroups of $GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$?

That is, for every $n$ and every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup $G$ of
$GL_n(\mathbb{C})$: for every $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$, is there a torsion-free subgroup $H$ of
$GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ (the same $n$) and a homomorphism $\varphi : G \to H$ with
$\varphi(g) \neq 1$? Here $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is modelled by `AlgebraicClosure ℚ`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.35» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) ℂ)), Group.FG G → IsTorsionFreeGroup G →
      ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
        ∃ H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)), IsTorsionFreeGroup H ∧
          ∃ φ : G →* H, φ g ≠ 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.35»

items: Q̄ is modelled as `AlgebraicClosure ℚ` rather than the relative closure `algebraicClosure ℚ ℂ` inside ℂ; all algebraic closures of ℚ are isomorphic, so GL_n(Q̄) and the statement are unaffected.

'Residually in the class 𝒳' is unfolded as: for every g ≠ 1 there exist a torsion-free subgroup H ≤ GL_n(Q̄) and a homomorphism φ : G →* H with φ g ≠ 1 (not required surjective). This is equivalent to the normal-subgroup/quotient formulation (and to the kernels intersecting trivially) because 𝒳 is closed under subgroups and isomorphism; the equivalence is explained in the module docstring.
Finite generation is `Group.FG G` on the subgroup coerced to a type (equivalent to `Subgroup.FG`).

The bespoke `IsTorsionFreeGroup` is generic; a reviewer may prefer moving it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib (not possible within this task's single-file constraint). The Kaplansky file in the repo uses `IsMulTorsionFree` for non-abelian groups, which appears to be the same pitfall; I did not touch it.
n = 0 is allowed; GL_0 is trivial so the statement is vacuous there, matching the source which places no restriction on n.

reviewer_notes: Key adjudication point: 'torsion-free' must mean 'only the identity has finite order'. Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` is the unique-roots property and differs for non-abelian groups (the existing FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean appears to have the same pitfall; not touched). `Monoid.IsTorsionFree` no longer exists in the pinned Mathlib (the Torsion.lean module docstring mentioning it is stale), so a bespoke `IsTorsionFreeGroup` was defined in the problem file; a reviewer may prefer moving it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib since it is generic. Modeling: Q̄ as `AlgebraicClosure ℚ` (c03's `algebraicClosure ℚ ℂ` would be equally faithful); residuality unfolded elementwise with a non-surjective hom into a torsion-free H ≤ GL_n(Q̄), equivalent to the kernel-intersection definition because the class is closed under isomorphism and subgroups; finite generation as `Group.FG ↥G`. Boundary: n = 0 and trivial G are vacuous (no g ≠ 1), no default-value artefacts. File compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; the three API lemmas are fully proven.
